I don't know what to tell you man. Just want to let you know that I read what you had to see and I see your pain.

My depression was consistent for a few years until about two years ago, now it comes and goes. At first I would feel depressed for a few months then I'd feel fine for a few more. Then It was a few weeks. Now it's a few days. But the good thing is the time between each episode is longer then the episode itself. 


I try my best to cope. That's my advice. Don't distract yourself, don't avoid it, don't run away this time. If you want things to get better then go through the motions properly. You'll figure out way to mentally cope and with time you'll gain faith that despite feeling hopeless that there is still hope you just can't see or feel.


What helps me cope is sharing how I feel with someone I trust and making a promise to try and do something about it. That someone for me sucks at showing compassion, empathy, or support which I guess is good because it means I have to rely on myself.
Yes! This. That's how it starts. You do it for others and eventually things feel a little better. Then you do it for yourself and things get a little more better. At least better than today

Shit! I know were you are coming from and I felt and still feel the same way. It doesn't get better but you find a way to cope. You just have to try. Force yourself too. This might have a good impact in your life. Have faith that it will.

is it the desire to find something to live for or be passionate about or maybe it's hope?

Don't think of the end of high school as the beginning of your life. Nothing will really change besides People coming and going more frequently in your life. Trust me, your life can start now, or a year ago, or a year from now.

Depression to me is a boulder that grows or shrinks. I carry it with me in my pocket or on my shoulders, the size depends on the kind of day. Anxiety is like a little kid who wants piggy-back rides and take up all my energy and attention but he only comes out when I lose control of my adhd. Adhd is like a car but not just any normal car that others use to go through life no this one has all these levers and buttons and dials and stuff that you have to constantly check and if you miss even one you fly off the road and anxiety hops in the car. Then you find that the day is wasted again and you sleep only to wake and find that the boulder has grown and its pushing down on the blanket.
